newsitem.title: USA: Cirrus reports big loss, to lay off 400.
newsitem.headline: Cirrus reports big loss, to lay off 400.

text.p: Cirrus Logic Inc on Wednesday reported an unexpected loss because of weak demand for its computer chips, and said it plans to lay off 400, or about 15 percent, of its workers.

Cirrus, a maker of electronic components for computers and telecommunication equipment said it had a fourth-quarter loss of $51.9 million, or $0.79 a share, compared with a loss of $88.4 million, or $1.38 a share, in the same quarter a year ago.
The loss in the most recent quarter included total charges of $34.5 million or a restructuring, the company said.
Cirrus said the loss from operations, not counting the charges, would have been about $1.5 million.
Wall Street expected Cirrus, based in Fremont, Calif., to earn $0.08 a share.
Fourth-quarter revenue fell 8.7 percent to $212.9 million from $233.1 million a year ago.
Cirrus specializes in making computer chips that handle the graphics and sound capabilies of computers, telecommunication equipment and consumer electronics.
In the past year, Cirrus' revenue has dropped because it has been slow to introduce advanced 3-D graphics chips, the components for which PC makers are clamouring.

Meanwhile, Intel Corp, the world's biggest computer chipmaker, has been making its Pentium microprocessors more efficient at handling the basic graphics functions of the PC, obviating the need for seperate chips from companies such as Cirrus.
"Our recovery has proceeded slower than expected," said Michael Hackworth, Cirrus president and chief executive.
To get sales going again, Cirrus said it will reshuffle its management team into an office of the president to make day-to-day operations more efficient.
Thomas Kelly, formerly the chief financial officer, was named chief operating officer. Ron Shelton, the former vice president of finance, will replace Kelly as CFO.
George Alexy, formerly the senior vice president of marketing, was named chief products and marketing officer, oveseeing product strategy and marketing.
Kelly said in an interview that Cirrus' goal is to be profitable again by the June quarter. The company also expects new graphics products to boost revenue by the September quarter, he said.
